title: All Namo Bharat RRTS Stations: Complete List with Facilities (2026)
description: Whether you are planning your first trip, trying to figure out which station has parking, or simply want to know what facilities to expect when you arrive, this is the only page you need
body:
The Delhi-Meerut Namo Bharat RRTS corridor is now fully operational across 82.15 km, connecting Sarai Kale Khan in South Delhi to Modipuram at the northern edge of Meerut. The complete corridor has 22 passenger stations plus 2 depot stations, totalling 24 points on the network (some sources count 25 including both depot variants). Whether you are planning your first trip, trying to figure out which station has parking, or simply want to know what facilities to expect when you arrive, this is the only page you need.

Every station is listed in order from Delhi to Meerut, with its structure type, opening date, available facilities, metro connections, and key information that is genuinely useful before you travel.

> Use the [MetroGuideIndia Namo Bharat route planner](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/) to find the exact route and fare between any two stations.

***

## A Quick Overview of the Full Corridor

The Namo Bharat corridor passes through three states and union territories: Delhi, then Uttar Pradesh through Ghaziabad district, then into Meerut district. Here is a snapshot of the network before we go [station by station.](https://metroguideindia.com/stations)

| Detail | Information |
| Total length | 82.15 km |
| Total passenger stations | 22 |
| Depot stations | 2 (Duhai Depot, Modipuram Depot) |
| Underground stations | 4 (Anand Vihar, Meerut Central, Bhaisali, Begumpul) |
| Elevated stations | 17 |
| At-grade stations | 1 (Duhai Depot) |
| Operates since | October 2023 (priority section), fully since February 2026 |
| Operating hours | 6:00 AM to 10:30 PM (Delhi to Meerut) |
| Train frequency | Approximately every 10 minutes |
| Top speed | 160 km/h |

For first and last train times from every station, check the [MetroGuideIndia timings page](https://metroguideindia.com/timings).

***

## Understanding the Two Services on This Corridor

Before reading the station list, it helps to know that two services share the same tracks and stations between Meerut South and Modipuram.

**Namo Bharat RRTS** runs the full length from Sarai Kale Khan to Modipuram at speeds up to 160 km/h. It stops at all major RRTS stations.

**Meerut Metro** is a separate service running between Meerut South and Modipuram at speeds up to 120 km/h, stopping at all 12 stations within Meerut city. RRTS trains pass through Meerut Metro-only stations without stopping.

This means stations like Partapur, Rithani, Shatabdi Nagar, Brahampuri, Meerut Central, Bhaisali, Begumpul, MES Colony, Daurli, and Meerut North are served by Meerut Metro trains only, not RRTS trains. If you are travelling within Meerut, you take the Meerut Metro. If you are travelling from Delhi to any Meerut station, you take Namo Bharat RRTS and change at Meerut South if needed.

***

## What Facilities Are Available at Every Station?

All Namo Bharat stations are built to a consistent NCRTC standard. Every station, regardless of size, provides:

- Full air conditioning throughout the station building
- Lifts and escalators for divyangjan (differently abled) accessibility
- Ticket vending machines (TVM) accepting UPI, card, and cash
- Drinking water facilities
- Washrooms on the concourse level
- CCTV surveillance throughout
- First aid availability
- Digital passenger information displays showing train timings, speed, and route
- QR code boarding support via the Namo Bharat Connect app

Where stations differ is in parking availability, the number of gates, connections to Delhi Metro or other transport, and whether they have premium lounges. Those differences are covered for each station below.

***

## All Namo Bharat RRTS Stations: Complete List

### Section 1: Delhi Stations (3 stations)

***

#### 1. Sarai Kale Khan

**Zone:** South East Delhi | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 22 February 2026

Sarai Kale Khan is the southern terminus of the Namo Bharat corridor and the most strategically significant station on the entire network. It is the planned originating point for three future RRTS corridors: Delhi-Meerut (operational), Delhi-Alwar (under planning), and Delhi-Sonipat-Panipat (under planning). The station has 6 platforms and 4 tracks, making it the most complex station structure on the corridor.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators to all levels
- Parking: Available
- Accessible (Divyangjan-friendly): Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Connections:**

- Delhi Metro Pink Line at Sarai Kale Khan station
- Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station (walkable)
- Sarai Kale Khan ISBT (inter-city buses)

**Who uses this station:** Long-distance travellers arriving at Nizamuddin, commuters from South Delhi, and passengers connecting from Pink Line metro.

> Check routes from Sarai Kale Khan using the [station route planner](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/).

***

#### 2. New Ashok Nagar

**Zone:** East Delhi | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 5 January 2025

New Ashok Nagar was the first Delhi station to open on the extended section beyond the original priority corridor, bringing Namo Bharat directly into the heart of East Delhi. It is an elevated station with side platforms and serves the densely populated New Ashok Nagar residential area.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: Yes (four-wheeler)
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Connections:**

- Delhi Metro Blue Line at New Ashok Nagar station (direct interchange)

**Who uses this station:** Residents of New Ashok Nagar, Mayur Vihar Phase 3, and nearby colonies commuting to Ghaziabad or Meerut. Also used by Blue Line metro users switching to RRTS.

***

#### 3. Anand Vihar

**Zone:** East Delhi | **Type:** Underground | **Opened:** 5 January 2025

Anand Vihar is the busiest interchange station on the entire Namo Bharat corridor. It sits 8 metres below ground level and connects with two Delhi Metro lines and two major rail/bus terminals above ground. If you are travelling from Central or West Delhi to Meerut, this is almost certainly where your RRTS journey begins.

The station has 3 lifts (1 platform access, 2 metro connections) and 5 escalators (3 platform access, 2 metro connections), plus 2 entry/exit gates. One entrance faces Chaudhary Charan Singh Marg and the other faces Anand Vihar Railway Station.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts: 3 (including metro interchange lifts)
- Escalators: 5
- Parking: TBC (underground station, limited)
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Connections:**

- Delhi Metro Blue Line at Anand Vihar station
- Delhi Metro Pink Line at Anand Vihar station
- Anand Vihar Railway Terminal (suburban and long-distance trains)
- Anand Vihar ISBT (inter-state buses)

**Who uses this station:** The largest mix of any station on the corridor. Workers, students, inter-city travellers, and anyone connecting from North or Central Delhi via metro.

For a detailed walkthrough of this transfer, read the [MetroGuideIndia guide on transferring from Delhi Metro to Namo Bharat at Anand Vihar](https://metroguideindia.com/blog).

***

### Section 2: Ghaziabad Stations (8 stations)

***

#### 4. Sahibabad

**Zone:** Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 21 October 2023

Sahibabad is historically significant as the station where Namo Bharat first began passenger services in October 2023. It was part of the original 17 km priority section and has handled the largest volume of passengers through the early phases of the corridor. The station serves the Vasundhara residential sectors and Sahibabad Industrial Area.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: Four-wheeler parking available
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Connections:**

- Sahibabad Bus Terminal (local and regional buses)

**Who uses this station:** Industrial workers from Sahibabad and residents of Vasundhara sectors 1-6.

***

#### 5. Ghaziabad

**Zone:** Ghaziabad City, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 21 October 2023

Ghaziabad is one of the most technically impressive stations on the corridor. It has 4 platform levels, 3 tracks, 5 entry/exit gates, 6 lifts, and 12 escalators, making it the most well-equipped mid-corridor station. It connects directly with Delhi Metro Red Line, giving Ghaziabad residents a seamless two-transit-network option.

Train services from Ghaziabad: first towards Delhi at 6:12 AM, last at 10:27 PM. Towards Meerut: first at 6:25 AM, last at 10:25 PM. Sunday services start later at approximately 8:12 AM.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts: 6
- Escalators: 12
- Entry/exit gates: 5
- Parking: Four-wheeler parking available
- Accessible: Yes (all levels)
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid
- NCRTC helpline: 9289928705

**Connections:**

- Delhi Metro Red Line at Shaheed Sthal (New Bus Adda) station

**Who uses this station:** Ghaziabad city residents, workers in the Patel Nagar industrial corridor, and Red Line metro users switching to RRTS.

***

#### 6. DPS Rajnagar (Guldhar)

**Zone:** Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 21 October 2023

Formerly known simply as Guldhar, this station was renamed DPS Rajnagar to reflect its proximity to the DPS Rajnagar school campus and the growing Rajnagar Extension residential zone. It is an elevated station serving the Meerut Road Industrial Area.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: Four-wheeler parking available
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Connections:** Auto-rickshaws and local buses on Meerut Road

**Who uses this station:** Industrial workers and residents of Rajnagar Extension, one of Ghaziabad's fastest-growing residential areas.

***

#### 7. Duhai

**Zone:** Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 21 October 2023

Duhai was the last station on the original priority section and marked the end of Phase 1 RRTS operations. The station is 215 metres long and 26 metres wide, with rail tracks at 24 metres above ground. It has 3 platforms, 4 gates, 8 lifts, and 8 escalators. Parking at Gate 3 only: 32 four-wheeler slots and 180 two-wheeler slots. Helmet storage is available at the station (Rs. 5 for up to 12 hours, Rs. 10 beyond 12 hours).

**Facilities:**

- Lifts: 8
- Escalators: 8
- Platforms: 3
- Gates: 4 (parking at Gate 3 only)
- Four-wheeler parking: 32 slots
- Two-wheeler parking: 180 slots
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid
- Eastern Peripheral Expressway (EPE) nearby

**Who uses this station:** Residents of Duhai and Morta village, and travellers connecting to the Eastern Peripheral Expressway.

***

#### 8. Duhai Depot

**Zone:** Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** At-Grade (ground level) | **Opened:** 21 October 2023

Duhai Depot is the maintenance hub for all Namo Bharat trainsets on the corridor. It is also a functioning passenger station, though less busy than others. Being at ground level, it has a different feel from the elevated stations. It serves as a terminal for some short-distance services within the priority section.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: Four-wheeler parking available
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Note:** This is primarily a depot with a functional passenger platform. Not all services stop here check the [Namo Bharat timings page](https://metroguideindia.com/timings) before planning to board here.

***

#### 9. Murad Nagar

**Zone:** Muradnagar, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 7 March 2024

Murad Nagar was part of the second phase expansion that opened in March 2024. The station serves the Muradnagar city on NH-34 (the Delhi-Meerut highway), a major industrial and residential town between Ghaziabad and Modinagar.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: Four-wheeler parking available
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Connections:** Auto-rickshaws and city buses to Muradnagar city centre

**Who uses this station:** Workers in Muradnagar's industrial estates and residents of Brij Vihar Colony and surrounding areas.

***

#### 10. Modinagar South

**Zone:** Modinagar, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 7 March 2024

Modinagar South serves the southern part of Modinagar town on NH-34. It opened alongside Murad Nagar and Modinagar North as part of the second phase expansion in March 2024.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: Four-wheeler parking available
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Who uses this station:** Residents of southern Modinagar and workers in the industrial belt along the Delhi-Meerut highway.

***

#### 11. Modinagar North

**Zone:** Modinagar, Ghaziabad, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 7 March 2024

Modinagar North serves the northern sections of Modinagar and sits near the ICICI Bank branch on GT Road. It is the last Ghaziabad district station before the corridor enters Meerut district.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: Four-wheeler parking available
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Who uses this station:** Modinagar North residents and travellers heading to industrial areas along GT Road near the Meerut border.

***

### Section 3: Meerut Stations (12 stations, including Meerut South)

From Meerut South onwards, both Namo Bharat RRTS and Meerut Metro trains share tracks and stations. RRTS trains stop only at Meerut South and Modipuram within Meerut. All intermediate stations are served by Meerut Metro only.

***

#### 12. Meerut South

**Zone:** Meerut, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 18 August 2024

Meerut South is the first Meerut station and the most important interchange point on the entire corridor for travellers from Delhi. This is where Namo Bharat RRTS passengers disembark and switch to Meerut Metro if their destination is within Meerut city. It has 3 tracks (1 side platform and 1 island platform), which allows both RRTS and Meerut Metro trains to operate simultaneously.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: Two-wheeler and four-wheeler parking both available
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Connections:** Meerut Metro (board here for all Meerut city stations)

**Who uses this station:** All Delhi commuters heading into Meerut city, and Meerut residents travelling to Delhi on RRTS.

> Plan your Delhi to Meerut route using the [Namo Bharat planner](https://metroguideindia.com/namo-bharat/).

***

#### 13. Partapur

**Zone:** Meerut, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 22 February 2026 **Service:** Meerut Metro only (RRTS trains pass through without stopping)

Partapur serves the Partapur area of Meerut, which has seen significant real estate growth since RRTS construction began. A proposed 750-acre township project in Partapur reflects the station's long-term development potential. RRTS trains pass through at 160 km/h without stopping here.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: Available (verify at station)
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

***

#### 14. Rithani

**Zone:** Meerut, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 22 February 2026 **Service:** Meerut Metro only

Rithani serves the Rithani suburb of Meerut along the RRTS corridor. Like other Meerut Metro stations within the city, RRTS trains run through at high speed without stopping.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: Available (verify at station)
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

***

#### 15. Shatabdi Nagar

**Zone:** Meerut, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 22 February 2026 **Service:** Meerut Metro only

Shatabdi Nagar serves Sector 5 of the MDA (Meerut Development Authority) zone. The station building is located underneath the platform level, with platform tracks at 24 metres above ground. It has 2 island platforms serving both RRTS tracks (for through trains) and Meerut Metro tracks.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: TBC (confirm at station)
- Accessible: Yes (TBC)
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

***

#### 16. Brahampuri

**Zone:** Meerut, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 22 February 2026 **Service:** Meerut Metro only

Brahampuri serves one of Meerut's older established localities. The station connects residents of the Brahampuri area to the rest of Meerut via Meerut Metro and to Delhi via changing to RRTS at Meerut South.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

***

#### 17. Meerut Central

**Zone:** Meerut City Centre, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Underground | **Opened:** 22 February 2026 **Service:** Meerut Metro only

Meerut Central is one of four underground stations on the entire corridor and serves the heart of Meerut city. Going underground through the old city centre was necessary due to the dense urban fabric and heritage zones. It is one of the most anticipated stations for Meerut residents, placing the rapid rail network right at the commercial and cultural core of the city.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes (underground to surface access)
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Who uses this station:** Shoppers, office workers, and residents of central Meerut. The station is a short walk from key commercial areas in the city centre.

***

#### 18. Bhaisali

**Zone:** Meerut, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Underground | **Opened:** 22 February 2026 **Service:** Meerut Metro only

Bhaisali is the second underground station within Meerut city, serving the Bhaisali locality. The 11.5 km underground stretch through Meerut, which includes Meerut Central, Bhaisali, Begumpul, and one additional station, was one of the most complex engineering challenges on the entire corridor.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes (underground access)
- Parking: TBC
- Accessible: Yes (TBC)
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

***

#### 19. Begumpul

**Zone:** Meerut, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Underground | **Opened:** 22 February 2026 **Service:** Meerut Metro only

Begumpul is the third underground station in Meerut, serving the Begum Pul area, which is one of the most historically significant locations in the city. The station has island platforms on 2 levels with 4 tracks total, accommodating both through RRTS tracks and Meerut Metro tracks.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: TBC
- Accessible: Yes (TBC)
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

***

#### 20. MES Colony

**Zone:** Meerut, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 22 February 2026 **Service:** Meerut Metro only

MES Colony serves the Military Engineering Services colony area of Meerut, a large cantonment-adjacent residential zone. The station is elevated and returns above ground after the underground city-centre section.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

***

#### 21. Daurli

**Zone:** Meerut, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 22 February 2026 **Service:** Meerut Metro only

Daurli serves the Daurli area in northern Meerut, providing connectivity to an area that previously had no rapid transit access. It is one of the newer residential zones on the outskirts of Meerut city.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

***

#### 22. Meerut North

**Zone:** Meerut, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 22 February 2026 **Service:** Meerut Metro only

Meerut North serves the northern reaches of Meerut city, an area that has expanded rapidly with new residential and commercial development. It is the second-to-last station before the Modipuram terminus.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

***

#### 23. Modipuram

**Zone:** Modipuram, Meerut, Uttar Pradesh | **Type:** Elevated | **Opened:** 22 February 2026

Modipuram is the northern terminus of both the Namo Bharat RRTS and the Meerut Metro. Located on National Highway 58, it marks the end of the 82.15 km corridor from Delhi. Both two-wheeler and four-wheeler parking are available here, making it a practical park-and-ride option for residents of Meerut North who prefer to drive to this station and take the train.

First train from Modipuram towards Delhi departs at 5:30 AM. Last train towards Delhi departs at 10:00 PM.

**Facilities:**

- Lifts and escalators: Yes
- Parking: Two-wheeler and four-wheeler parking both available
- Accessible: Yes
- Washrooms, drinking water, first aid

**Who uses this station:** Residents of Modipuram and surrounding areas of north Meerut, and anyone travelling the full corridor length from Meerut to Delhi.

> For the full fare from Modipuram to any station, use the [MetroGuideIndia fare guide](https://metroguideindia.com/fares).

***

## Parking at Namo Bharat Stations: Summary Table

One of the most searched questions about Namo Bharat stations is where you can park your vehicle. Here is a summary of all stations with confirmed parking.

| Station | Two-Wheeler Parking | Four-Wheeler Parking |
| Sarai Kale Khan | Available | Available |
| New Ashok Nagar | Not confirmed | Yes |
| Anand Vihar | Limited/TBC | Limited/TBC |
| Sahibabad | Not listed | Yes |
| Ghaziabad | Not listed | Yes |
| DPS Rajnagar (Guldhar) | Not listed | Yes |
| Duhai | Yes (180 slots, Gate 3) | Yes (32 slots, Gate 3) |
| Duhai Depot | Not listed | Yes |
| Murad Nagar | Not listed | Yes |
| Modinagar South | Not listed | Yes |
| Modinagar North | Not listed | Yes |
| Meerut South | Yes | Yes |
| Modipuram | Yes | Yes |
| Meerut city stations | TBC / verify at station | TBC / verify at station |

For stations where parking details are marked TBC, check the Namo Bharat Connect app or contact the station helpline (9289928705 for Ghaziabad) before your visit.

***

## Delhi Metro Connections at Namo Bharat Stations

Four Namo Bharat stations connect directly with the Delhi Metro network. These interchange points are the entry and exit gateways for most Delhi commuters using RRTS.

| Namo Bharat Station | Delhi Metro Line | Delhi Metro Station Name |
| Sarai Kale Khan | Pink Line | Sarai Kale Khan |
| New Ashok Nagar | Blue Line | New Ashok Nagar |
| Anand Vihar | Blue Line + Pink Line | Anand Vihar |
| Ghaziabad | Red Line | Shaheed Sthal (New Bus Adda) |

If you are coming from Central Delhi (Rajiv Chowk, Kashmere Gate, New Delhi station), the fastest route is usually Yellow or Blue Line to Anand Vihar, then Namo Bharat from Anand Vihar station.

For a detailed guide on the transfer process, visit the [MetroGuideIndia Namo Bharat RRTS Complete Guide](https://metroguideindia.com/blog/namo-bharat-rrts-guide-2026-routes-stations-timings-fare-complete-travel-guide.html).

***

## Underground Stations: What to Know

Four stations on the corridor are underground, forming part of an 11.5 km underground stretch. These stations have a distinct atmosphere from the elevated ones and require a bit more navigation.

**Anand Vihar (Delhi):** 8 metres below ground, two island platforms. This is the most complex station on the corridor. Three lifts and five escalators connect street level to platforms. Two entry gates: one facing Chaudhary Charan Singh Marg, one facing Anand Vihar Railway Station.

**Meerut Central:** Serves the commercial heart of Meerut city. Being underground through a dense urban area, this station took the longest to build and is among the most eagerly awaited by Meerut residents.

**Bhaisali:** Underground station serving the Bhaisali locality. Part of the 11.5 km underground segment through Meerut.

**Begumpul:** Underground station at Begum Pul, one of Meerut's historic localities. Has 2 platform levels and 4 tracks to accommodate both Meerut Metro and RRTS through-traffic.

At all underground stations, lifts and escalators connect every level. If you have heavy luggage or require accessible travel, use the lifts rather than escalators.

***

## Common Questions About Namo Bharat Stations

### How many stations does Namo Bharat have in total?

The Namo Bharat Delhi-Meerut corridor has 22 passenger stations and 2 depot stations (Duhai Depot and Modipuram Depot). Of the 22 passenger stations, 17 are elevated, 4 are underground, and 1 is at ground level.

### Which Namo Bharat stations are underground?

Four stations are underground on the corridor: Anand Vihar in Delhi, and Meerut Central, Bhaisali, and Begumpul within Meerut city.

### Which Namo Bharat station connects to Delhi Metro?

Four stations connect to Delhi Metro: Sarai Kale Khan (Pink Line), New Ashok Nagar (Blue Line), Anand Vihar (Blue and Pink Lines), and Ghaziabad (Red Line).

### Do all Namo Bharat stations have parking?

No. Parking is confirmed at Sahibabad, Ghaziabad, Guldhar, Duhai, Duhai Depot, Murad Nagar, Modinagar South, Modinagar North, Meerut South, and Modipuram. Anand Vihar, being underground in a dense urban area, has limited or no parking. For Meerut city stations, verify parking availability directly at the station.

### Do Namo Bharat RRTS trains stop at all Meerut city stations?

No. RRTS trains stop only at Meerut South and Modipuram within Meerut. All other Meerut stations (Partapur, Rithani, Shatabdi Nagar, Brahampuri, Meerut Central, Bhaisali, Begumpul, MES Colony, Daurli, Meerut North) are served exclusively by Meerut Metro trains.

### What is the first station on Namo Bharat from Delhi?

The first station on the Namo Bharat corridor when travelling from Delhi is Sarai Kale Khan, which is the Delhi terminus located in South East Delhi near Hazrat Nizamuddin Railway Station.

### What is the last station on Namo Bharat?

Modipuram is the northern terminus of the Namo Bharat corridor, located in Modipuram town in Meerut district on National Highway 58.

### Are all Namo Bharat stations accessible for differently abled passengers?

Yes. All Namo Bharat stations are built to divyangjan-accessible standards, with lifts, ramps, tactile paths, and accessible washrooms at every station. The stations are NCRTC-operated and follow national accessibility guidelines.
